correctness.rationale: The two exponentials in cos(x+y) give exactly the n↔n+2 matrix entries ε exp[-s(n+1)^2]/2. Gaussian diagonal congruence yields I+(εe^t/2)J; integrating against trigonometric-polynomial densities by Riemann sums and, conversely, truncating the absolutely convergent Fourier series proves equivalence to all finite Gram tests. The growing two-index minor, the free adjacency spectrum, and the bipartite compact spectrum respectively yield the three sharp cutoffs. At the common-time boundary the free edge has no ℓ² eigenvector. At the unequal-time compact boundary a nonzero extremal eigenvector, iterated along m Jacobi edges, decays as O_m(exp[-m(s−t)(|n|−2m)^2]); choosing m(s−t)>t/2 makes its inverse-Gaussian-weighted coefficients smooth and summable. The resulting measure annihilates kernel sections since its energy is zero, but no nonzero finite atomic measure can have Fourier coefficients tending to zero (its Cesàro mean square is the sum of squared atomic masses). This proves the claimed strictness/density split. For decreasing norm, evaluate the less-decayed block on the strictly positive Perron vector of the more-decayed one; at least one edge improves strictly. The endpoint limits follow from finite free-path comparisons at zero and uniform deletion of all but the central odd edge at infinity. An independent finite rational calculation checked all three parity comparisons, with omitted tails bounded by their absolute row sums: odd >1.5254155 vs even <1.5254140; even >1.3750732 vs odd <1.3748651; odd >1.1464312 vs even <1.1393045. Norm continuity gives two disjoint crossing intervals.
residual_risks: Neither an exhaustive crossing count nor a finite-configuration conditioning estimate was tested or claimed.
